The identification of critical parameters and their optimized setup is also an important task for the DoE. Robustness and a high stability are also possible responses for such an analysis.

articleTitle: Implementation of Ecological Technologies in Electronics Industry based on RESPLATEPE Research Project
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The paper presents the applied research performed in the frame of RESPLATEPE Romanian CEEX national project destined to implementation of ecological technologies in electronics industry, based on based on RoHS and WEEE directives [3]. The work represents a multi-criteria approach in electronics packaging and emphasizes the activity of eight research partners involved in various phases of electronic manufacturing process. Under work are activities regarding electrical, rheological, climatic, and mechanical testing of experimental ecological modules and structures (the relative humidity controller presented in this contribution being one example) developed in the first stage. After them, the team will perform investigations of signals parameters, environmental factors and interconnection technologies influences on ecological electronic modules developed or destined for future development.

articleTitle: Cost Effective Component Placement Quality Measure through Pre-reflow AOI and SPC Tools - one step to the DPC
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) is a useful tool for assessing workmanship compliance in production PCB assembly environments. With advanced lighting, optics, and image processing capabilities, the machines greatly enhance inspection repeatability, accuracy and throughput. The in-line automatic optical inspection machines usually are not accurate enough to measure the Cmk of the component placement machines, but the x,y shift and the rotation of the components could be measured with circa 25 mum precision.

articleTitle: The Center for Non-Destructive Nano Evaluation of Electronic Packaging (nanoEVA), a New Research Facility in Dresden
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The challenge of nano packaging requires new non-destructive evaluation (NDE) techniques to detect and characterize very small defects like Kirkendall voids or micro cracks. Imaging technologies with resolutions in the sub-micron range are desired. Possible evaluation methods are for example x-ray microscopy, x-ray tomography, ultrasonic microscopy and thermal microscopy. However, techniques with this resolution can not be found on the market. The Center for Non-Destructive Nano Evaluation (nanoeva) is launched to develop this equipment jointly with the electronics industry and to transfer the knowledge to colleagues in industry and research institutions. The new center is a common organization of Fraunhofer IZFP-D and the Centre of Microtechnical Manufacturing (ZμP) of the Technische Universität Dresden.

articleTitle: Hardware Design for Noise Reduction in Data Acquisition Modules
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In the introduction of this paper are briefly presented the most important sources of noise in data acquisition modules and classical techniques for reducing this noise. Are clarified the types of input configurations available on data acquisition devices and are explained how should be choused and used the best configuration for an application. Also are analyzed the interference noise pick up mechanisms and the methods to minimize interference noise by proper cabling and shielding. After that it is described a new method of noise reduction, in which a square-wave signal is modulated with signal from sensor (input signal) and then it is applied at instrumentation amplifier. The amplified signal is modulated again with the same signal type before analog to digital conversion. The noise and offset voltage that appears due amplifier and from external sources are modulated only once by the final multiplier and translated to the harmonics. By using a low-pass filter, results a clear output signal with reduced noise components. Further low pass filtering it is necessary for eliminating the residual offset voltages that appears due to the use of this technique.

articleTitle: Virtual instrument designed for dynamic testes of electro-hydraulic devices
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The dynamic testes of electro-hydraulic devices, realized in the laboratory of Hydraulics and Pneumatics Research Institute (INOE 2000 - IHP), used the latest data acquisition system which for have been developed dedicated virtual instruments. The dynamic behavior of electro-hydraulic devices is evaluated by the use of two methods: the transient response method and the frequency response method. Usually, the data acquisition system used to these types of tests contains wave signal generator, a current feedback amplifier, and hydraulic cylinder, sensors for monitoring the displacement, pressure, flow and FFT analyzer or oscilloscope. Using virtual instruments these devices are replaced by a computer that has a data acquisition board inside and the applications developed.

articleTitle: Using Of Distributed And Parallel Computing (DPAC) In The Manufacturing Control
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Parallel and distributed computing infrastructure is increasingly being embraced in the context of manufacturing applications, including real-time scheduling. The paper present the design and implementation of one such framework than can work on the Internet, with applications in automation (manufacturing). The architecture of Distributed and PArallel Compuring framework (DPAC) has the goal of harnessing the Internet's vast, growing computational capacity for ultra-large, coarse-grained parallel applications. DPAC idea is to bring together diverse, heterogeneous, geographically distributed computing environments in order to attack large-scale computing problems. In paper is describe an implementation and present case studies showing the effectiveness in solving complex combinatorial optimization problems in the context of manufacturing systems.

articleTitle: Advanced tunable protective structure against electrostatic discharge
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: ESD (electrostatic discharge) protection structures act as a protection of integrated circuits against parasitic electrostatic discharge events. They are located on input or output (I/O) pads. The use of such structures provides better robustness against ESD but also a number of secondary parasitic effects which limit the circuit performance. These effects, for example, limit the bandwidth of processed signals, causes bigger noise or lower gain. Among often used structures belong structures known as SCR (silicon controlled rectifier). Structures like SCR have some disadvantages, therefore they can not be universally usable. This text is dealing with advanced SCR structure, which overcomes disadvantages of conventional SCR protection cell. Physical principle of this new structure allows required features tuning by geometrical adjustments only..

articleTitle: Semantically described services in the Enterprise Application Integration
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Supporting the everyday management and working processes of an organization is hard to imagine without software systems today. Enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM), computer aided engineering (CAE), computer aided design (CAD), etc. systems can be found everywhere in working processes of organizations. Although these systems provide a lot of information they aren't able to satisfy the emerging need for collaborating with other systems. Enterprise application integration (EAI) can solve this problem. In this paper we give an example how to increase the effectiveness of integration by applying semantically described services. A working demo example will also be introduced which were designed and developed at our department.

articleTitle: Wetting Force Measurement of the Different Types of Solders and Testing Materials
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: We have used one of the most commonly used wetability evaluation methods - wetting balance (meniscograph) method to measure the wetting force. We have made a modification of the measuring equipment to measure a less quantity of the solder. We have measured a combination of different types of the lead and lead-free solders and different types of the testing materials. The measurement was carried out on nine different types of solders (Sn63Pb37, Sn95Sb5, Sn95Sb3,5Cu1,5, Sn96Ag4, Sn95,5Ag3,8Cu0,7, Sn97Bi2Cu1, Sn97Cu3, Sn99Cu1, Sn99,75), three types of testing materials (copper, nickel and brass) and three types of fluxes. All measurements nine solders ware measured in ambient atmosphere and two lead-free solders were (Sn96Ag4, Sn95,5Ag3,8Cu0,7) measured in inert atmosphere. The results of measurements we classified into the table according to he shape of wetting curve and according to the visual control.

articleTitle: Digital PWM control implementation for System on Chip devices
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Nowadays, PWM control circuits are usually embedded into a microprocessor or a system-on-chip core. It is up to designer's choice to evaluate precisely the quantity of resources required for such an implementation and how much the control function and/or the power topology influence this decision. The paper proposes a method of evaluation for resource usage in case of different control functions for a PWM controlled switch power supply. Starting from the basic functional equations for a closed loop PWM controlled system, calculations and simulations steps can provide a solution for digital PWM implementation.

articleTitle: Laser Characterization of the Periodic Line-Space Micro/Nano Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Recent advances in micro/nanotechnology devices have demonstrated periodic line-space structure with dimensions of order less than ten nm. Laser scatterometry is a noncontact measurement method for collecting and analyzing of scattered light from the structures. Methods using laser scatterometry can characterize periodic line-space structures. The objective of this paper is three-fold: (1) characterization of laser beam quality which is used for optical metrology; (2) optical characterization of periodic line-space structures; (3) some conclusions regarding experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Reliability of Operation of Single Chip Microprocessor with Watchdog in Thermal Stress Conditions
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The temperature influence (especially their irregular distribution in the digital chip structure) on proper operation of the microprocessor system has been presented in the paper. As the results of non-uniform heating of silicon structure the incorrect operation of selected functional blocks of single chip microprocessor can be observed. Especially, the circuits which operation is independent on global clock of the whole logic structure are endangered on such phenomena. The good example can be block which controls the correctness of program running - its operation is dependent on correct working of independent internal generator. In reality (especially where temperature changes are sudden - e.g. turn on of microprocessor system) the systems of temperature correction does not operate properly and watching time is changed. As result the incorrect clearing signal can be generated.

articleTitle: Digital technique of circuit's analyses
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Circuit simulation is a powerful tool for circuit design and evaluation, and, over the years, many computer programs have been developed for this purpose. Most of these programs are designed so that the commonly used circuit elements are incorporated within the program, and the user can call them in the circuit file following certain syntax rules and keywords specified by the program designer. However, incorporation of a new element by the user is generally impossible, or only allowed in a limited manner by modification of the model equations of an existing element. This situation reduces the flexibility offered to the user for solving new problems.

articleTitle: High Frequency Behavior of Microstrip Lines on Composite Photopolymer Substrate
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Recent trends in PCB design are microvia technologies. Several manufacturing processes are used for microvia technologies. PhotoVia is the method where the photoimageable dielectric materials have to be used. This paper deals with high frequency behavior of microstrip lines created on special photodielectric substrates. Scattering parameters are possible to use to describe high frequency properties of microstrip lines. The results of scattering parameters measurement of microstrip lines on photodielectric substrates are compared with microstrip lines on FR-4 or ARLON ADxxxx substrates.

articleTitle: Viscosity of Polymer Paste Materials for Electronics
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The article is focused on properties of polymer paste materials these were applied in electronics production. Viscosity of such materials is investigated in particular. Samples of electrically conductive adhesives and electrically conductive pastes for screen printing were chosen for experiment. Viscosity of such materials is influenced on properties and quality final thick film structure. Viscosity was measured by method using the rotational viscometer. The dependence of viscosity on temperature was analyzed.

articleTitle: The Non-Linear Electro-Ultrasonic Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The ultrasonic signal is familiarly used in non-destructive spectroscopy. The paper presents the new method of the non-destructive testing procedure of conductive materials. The non-linear electro-ultrasonic spectroscopy is new method which has higher sensitivity and range of using than common ultrasonic testing method which has many problems. We are applying two signals: (i) ultrasonic signal with frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</sub> and (ii) harmonic AC electric signal of frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub>. The ultrasonic phonons modulate the transport of electrons through the structure and in the vicinity of defects and un-homogeneities the intermodulation signal is created. The frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> of the intermodulation signal is given by the superposition or subtraction of exciting frequencies f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</sub> and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub>.The main advantage of this method is the detection of electrical signal with frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> which is different from frequencies of excitation signals. We are measuring the signal with frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>=f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">U</sub>-f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub>.

articleTitle: Statistical Inspection of a Workplace for Adhesive Assembly
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Quality of a workplace for adhesive assembly has been examined using acceptance sampling. The goal of the work has been to find our whether dispensing of electrically conductive adhesive makes forming of adhesive joints with sufficient reliability and repeatability possible. Adhesive joints have been fabricated by adhesive assembly of jumpers. Four types of adhesives, one of an acrylate type and three of an epoxy type with Ag filler have been used for testing. Joints resistances have been measured by a four-point method. Acceptance sampling by attributes has been used for statistical inspection. Acceptance plan has been calculated. It has been found that the workplace does not give results with sufficient quality.

articleTitle: Characterization of solar cells contacts deposited by direct writing approach
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The main aim of this paper is show capability of direct write technology. This method is suitable to produce small amount prototypes of circuits on inorganic substrates such as ceramic or silicon (no need of screens). We will show the deposition of contacts on solar cells. Contacts were analysed and compared with standard screen printed contacts.

articleTitle: Development of novel room temperature ozone sensors for health and safety applications
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: A new type of highly sensitive ozone (O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) metal oxide gas sensor has been developed. Various mixtures of ln<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, ZnO and SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> were deposited on alumina substrates containing indigitated electrodes by means of vacuum thermal evaporation (VTE). Deposition rate of the sensing layer was varied from 0.3 nm/s-1.4 nm/s. The highest sensitivity of the sensors was found at a deposition rate of 1.2 nm/s-1.4 nm/s. In addition the O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> sensors were found to perform best with a 40 nm thick sensing layer. With such sensors, environmentally relevant ozone concentrations can be measured (0-500 ppb (parts per billion)). Different combinations of this material were investigated and compared focusing on the sensitivity and performance when exposed to ozone. Most of the current metal oxide ozone sensors on the market have the disadvantage of requiring operation at elevated temperatures (200degC-600degC). Room temperature operation has some major advantages over elevated temperature operation such as, reduced fabrication costs, reduced operating costs, as well as ease of implementation into portable/handheld devices.

articleTitle: UV Solar radiation monitoring system based on the PMA1111 (UVA) and PMA1102 (UVB) sensors
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The paper presents an original solution for the development of a monitoring system for the solar UV radiation, having the necessary functions to inform the population of the UV solar radiation levels, as instantaneous values. Moreover the data supplied by the system can be the base of long term studies on solar radiation levels. The paper also contains experimental data obtained during the conception and testing phases of the proposed solution. Lately, the UV radiation levels have become a major problem for the majority of the countries, a fact that imposed an earlier and active involvement in finding a solution for this problem. This led to the birth of similar devices on the international market. The main purpose of the development of this monitoring system was to offer the local market a cheaper but similarly complex device with the ones from the international market. The purposed monitoring system contains particular functions with customization possibilities and offers the later solution of a multi-point network system with server based data management.

articleTitle: Qualification of Organic Substrate Materials for High Temperature Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach in electronics packaging for high temperature environments. Especially electronics for automotive applications require effective packaging solutions which can withstand high temperatures. For these extreme conditions a new attempt, based on detailed knowledge about thermo-mechanical behavior of the utilized organic substrate materials, is necessary. Therefore different Thermal Analysis methods like Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) and Thermo Mechanical Analysis (TMA) can be used to characterize material behavior and material degradation under diverse stress conditions. The DMA is a method which uses cyclic deformations for gaining information about visco-elastic material properties and to detect material phase transitions. The TMA reveals information about expansion properties and phase transitions as well. A short introduction to the difficulties in parameter extracting and interpreting is given. Subsequently results for epoxy based substrate materials which were exposed to thermal stress are presented. Effects for detectable property shifts and polymer degradation are described.

articleTitle: Signals Analysis of the Fluorescence Emission
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper describes tests of detector electronics for a prototype optical pick-up designed to be used in a hyper CD drive with Terabyte storage capacity. The requirements for testing detectors and the experimental setup are discussed in details. As a detector a PIN Quadrant will be used. The characteristics of Quadrant detector such as bandwidth and noise will be analyzed and compared with the best results in data storage industry. The goal is to select an appropriate Quadrant for detecting a fluorescence laser pulse from recorded medium. Using a digital oscilloscope and a spectrum analyzer it is possible to study the characteristics of detector electronics.

articleTitle: Sensorless Brushless Motor Controller With N-MOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: One of the major concerns at world wide level today is the reduction of power consumption in any form possible. Many types of fuels, engines and technology had been developed taking in consideration as main parameter: efficiency. In this idea an outstanding high efficiency motor is the brushless one. Unfortunately the down sides of this motor are not few: difficult to start when it needs to drive a large torque, efficiency is strongly related with resistance of power transistors in switch ON (conduction) state, and for high power plant located in small volume enclosure the thermal management becomes an important issue. As consequences to reduce as much as possible the issues mentioned it is necessary to use a proper controller between DC power source and motor. The controller is the one that is converting the DC power into the three phase signal needed by the motor. The main parameters that were investigated for improvement where: low resistance in conduction state-to ensure high efficiency of the motor, wide range of rotation speed to control with maximum torque -to ensure rigorous starting of the engine. The result is equipment that uses latest technology in power conversion and packaging, able to satisfy the highest demands.

articleTitle: Assembly Problems in Lead-free and Mix Production
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Some electronic assemblers are faced to face with the necessity to use heterogeneous assembly of both very large and very small components on the same board and mix tin-lead and lead free soldering technology. Authors try to solve the problems with pick and place very small components by special design of stencil and adjust printing and assembly parameters. The solution of the soldering problems they try to solve by optimization the soldering profiles for mix technology.

articleTitle: Measurement of Nonlinearity as a Diagnostic Tool for Quality Determination of Lead-free Solder Joints
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: At present there are directions RoHS-WEEE in European Union which restrict the use of certain hazardous substances in new electric and electronic products. Therefore mass usage of lead-free soldering in electronic production started. A typical alloy for lead-free soldering is based on Sn, Ag and Cu (SAC). For the most of types of lead-free solders is necessary to use technological process of soldering in reduced oxygen concentration atmosphere for improvement of wettability of soldered surfaces. Quality of these soldered joints is evaluated according of their electrical and mechanical properties. This paper is focused on measurement of nonlinearity, electrical resistance and mechanical strength. Especially evaluation of nonlinearity as a diagnostic tool for the prediction of solder joints reliability has been tested. Also effect of different surface finish of PCBs and influence of reduced oxygen concentration on quality of joints has been examined.

articleTitle: High Energy Pulse Generator in Reliability Researches of Thick-Film Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In modern electronic microcircuits the intended and unintentional dynamic changes of the temperature (for example caused be electrical signals) are very often observed. The good knowledge about these phenomena is the basis of lifetime and reliability determination in the real-world operating conditions. The presented pulse generator is very useful in researches connected with such problems especially with reliability researches. It allows generating the high-energy pulses with short time duration. The special solution of the discharge circuit has been applied in the generator - it causes the precise realization of voltage and current measurements of the discharge pulse. Using of the microprocessor control system allows to introduce the additional functions which are very useful for users. Additionally, it is equipped in many constructional solutions, which are useful for different kinds of laboratory investigations.

articleTitle: Fermi Level Position in the Cadmium Telluride Detector
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The Fermi level position behavior in the CdTe single crystal was analyzed. The CdTe sample is p-type with the acceptor concentration N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub> =10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. The CdTe sample transport characteristics were measured during time period of 17 hours. During this measurement the temperature was increased from 300 K up to 400 K and then decreased down to 300 K. The Fermi level position was calculated for this measurement. Calculations show that the Fermi level position doesn 't change simultaneously with the temperature changing. The holes concentration depends on the Fermi level. The closer the Fermi level to the acceptor level, the higher the holes concentration.

articleTitle: Resistance of BGA Contacts During Reliability Tests
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper shows the latest results of lead-free BGA solder joints investigations performed in frame of GrenRoSE Project financed by EC. First part is devoted for resistance measurement of BGA256r (pitch 1.27) contacts. Resistance was measured during mechanical bending tests. Resistance of lead-free and lead-containing BGA contacts during reliability test and reliability of these contacts were compared. Second part is devoted for reliability assessment of solder joints of BGA packages, type CSP84 (pitch 0.5 mm), BGA100 (pitch 0.8 mm), BGA144 and BGA676 (pitch 1.0 mm), BGA272 (pitch 1.27 mm), lead-free and lead-containing. These packages were tested by thermal shocks according to IPC 9701A and EN 62137 and mechanical fatigue test by bending on mechanical stand.

articleTitle: Effect of Lead-free Conductive Thick Film Materials on Ultrasonic Wire Bondability
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The extent of wire bond ability of thick and thin film materials is determined by their mechanical properties. In the year 2006, there were introduced in EU new legislative regulations RoHS for materials used in electronics that have to exclude using of some chemicals, as for example Pb. This paper deals with verification of bondability and reliability of wire bonding ultrasonic process for lead-free thick film conductive materials. There were used some mechanical tests in the combination with temperature cycle aging. This testing was applied on two conductive thick film materials, one old and other lead free new.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of the PCB's Behaviour under the Mechanical Stress
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The aspect of the vulnerability of electronics generated by the mechanical causes requires a special analyzing and testing effort of the packages in the context of each different particular application. The main goal of this paper is to present the numerical evaluation by finite element analysis of the common class of PCBs under the mechanical stress. This work contributes to the study of packaged electronics vulnerability by comparing the numerical results with experimental tests.

articleTitle: Roadmap of Lead-free Soldering
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: In this presentation is profiled in short form roadmap of Lead-free soldering process, which has a general character and sums the most important parameters and factors that concern achievements of good solder joint quality. This course is involved in the 5th semester of the Bachelor study program as well in extended form in Master Study program at Brno University of Technology but it has a general force for electrical engineering education. Curriculum is intended as well as an orientation for companies planning to go lead-free. Results assume many articles and works presented by IMAPS, IEEE and NEMI, as well some projects (ELFNET), journals (SMT, SMT&Packaging) and companies presentation (ERSA). The curriculum is targeted to the general population of electrical engineering students and industry part time students as well as all technicians working in microelectronics assembly technology sector. The course presents the concepts of the complete area of lead free soldering, that means includes mostly part of factors and parameters that might to affect the quality and reliability of solder joint.

articleTitle: Thermal Shift in Electrical Behavior of Substrate Materials with Improved Flame Resistance
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: A halogen-free class of materials for PCB substrate was considered here, with good properties of electrical safety of flammability. The electrical properties of this class of materials were analyzed in this paper by calculating the HF values for the effective permittivity of these materials and illustrating its evolution with frequency and temperature. We have used a CAD technique which was developed by conceiving an algorithm based on physical considerations for effective permittivity calculation, with help of a high level computing program, specialized in HF and microwave range. The resonant electrical behavior of the considered materials was illustrated and our new contribution was to compute the thermal shift of these resonances for each material. Results interpretations and comments are also available, to explain the thermal shift link with materials components structure. This study continues our work in the field of new PCB materials characterization. Similar analyzes were performed by us for other halogen-free PCB material classes and our intention is to develop our data base for concluding finally on materials properties and their HF and temperature behavior for materials exploitation optimization and completing the electric compatibility rules.

articleTitle: Electrically Loaded Adhesive Bonds Formed on Different Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: Bonds of three types of electrically conductive adhesives with isotropic electrical conductivity have been formed on three types of surfaces - Cu; immerse Au and Sn (HAL). Epoxy resin types of adhesives with Ag flakes have been used. The bonds have been fabricated by assembly of jumpers. Two types of electrical load have been applied: DC current 1A and rectangular current pulses with the frequency of 500 Hz, mark-space ratio 1:1 and amplitude of 1A. The resistances, nonlinearity and noise of the bonds have been measured. It has been found that quality of the bonds on Sn surface finish is unacceptable through instability and level of measured parameters. The resistances and nonlinearity of the bonds formed on Au surface finish have been higher in comparison with those measured on Cu pads; noise have been comparable. Both types of the current load have caused low changes of all parameters tested.

articleTitle: Chip Power Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: This paper describes recent developments made to the finite element modeling of wire bonding interconnection, extending its capability to handle viscoplastic behavior. In this project a test system to be used in investigation and research on reliability of interconnections in integrated circuits and printed circuit boards will be developed and realised. Especially the reliability of interconnections of semiconductor chips under high current regime until 10 A, or more, is emphasised. This study discusses the analysis methodologies as implemented in the ANSYS finite element simulation software tool. The aim of this paper is to improve reliability of chip interconnection and to increase durability of these structures.

articleTitle: Simulation of an image acquisition system
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to simulate in images the functionality of an image acquisition system. The system consists of an object, the Cook Tyler triplet lenses, the optical part of the CCD, the Bayer RGB color filter array and analog to digital conversion. We present in images the transformation of the object input image as it passes through such a system.

articleTitle: Wide-band Antireflection Coatings upon Si/HgCdTe Photosensitive Structures for Middle Wavelength IR
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The investigation deals with problems of computer-aided design of wide-band antireflection coatings for semiconductor photo receiving devices (discrete photo receivers, IR photo receivers' arrays) based on HgCdTe photosensitive material with optical windows from Si for the middle wavelength infrared spectral region (3 mum - 5 mum). Wide-band antireflection multilayer structures from two materials transparent in upper mentioned spectral region with high and low refractive index are designed and compared.

articleTitle: Sensors for Obstacle Detection - A Survey
publicationTitle: 2007 30th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology (ISSE)
abstract: The obstacle detection field is a very broad one and a lot of obstacle detection systems have been developed in the last years in this domain. We tried to identify the main character of an obstacle detection system from the ruttier scene. Thus, we classified the main types of sensors from this field in passive (visible and infrared spectrum camera) and active (radar, laser-scanner, sonar) sensors and we made a survey in this domain. After a short presentation of every type of sensor, we presented another current and fancy solution for an obstacle detection system: the fusion of different sensor together. Almost all obstacle detection systems use a combination of passive-active technology, and in general the best solution is obtained using a vision system combined with a distance sensor like radar or laser. Maybe the most low-priced system is one combining only vision systems, but the inconvenient in this case is the lack of distance information.
